questions.q: What is the capstone project's overall goal?
options: To learn an entirely new set of cloud services not covered elsewhere in the course
To design a small office network, connect it to cloud resources, and diagnose a connectivity problem using concepts from across the whole course
To memorize additional DNS record types
To replace the course's final exam with a group project
questions.explain: The capstone combines subnetting, DNS/DHCP, firewalls, VPNs, troubleshooting methodology, and cloud concepts from every earlier chapter into one project.

questions.q: Which chapter's concepts does the office's subnet plan for ~50 devices rely on?
options: Chapter 1 — Hardware, Operating Systems & Software
Chapter 2 — Networking Foundations (IP addressing, subnets, CIDR)
Chapter 6 — Cloud Fundamentals
Chapter 7 — Capstone
questions.explain: Subnetting and CIDR, covered in Chapter 2, are what a local addressing plan for the office's roughly 50 devices is built on.

questions.q: What is the reported symptom of the broken scenario?
options: No devices on the office network can get an IP address
File shares and printers work, but reaching the cloud-hosted inventory system times out
The office has no internet connectivity at all
The inventory system itself is down for every office
questions.explain: Local resources (file shares, printers) work fine, but reaching the cloud-hosted inventory system specifically times out — and that system is confirmed healthy from other offices.

questions.q: Why is a VPN included in the office network's requirements?
options: To block all outbound internet traffic
To provide a secure way to reach cloud-hosted checkout and inventory systems without exposing the office directly to the internet
To assign IP addresses to local devices
To replace the need for a firewall entirely
questions.explain: The VPN gives the office a secure path to cloud-hosted systems, consistent with the VPN concepts covered in Chapter 4, without exposing the office network directly to the public internet.

questions.q: What troubleshooting approach is this capstone expected to use when diagnosing the broken connection?
options: Randomly restarting devices until something works
The systematic identify, isolate, test, resolve, document methodology from Chapter 5
Calling the cloud provider's support line immediately
Rebuilding the entire network from scratch
questions.explain: The capstone explicitly expects the structured troubleshooting methodology taught in Chapter 5, rather than ad hoc guessing.
